title: Hekko
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Understand Hekko's name
levels.focus: use word parts and story context
levels.teaching_goal: Use word parts and context to explain the meaning of a cultural game name.

guided_check.teaching_block: Some words carry meaning through smaller parts. In the Hekko story, the name connects a challenge with a tiger figure from the game tradition.
guided_check.passage: A teacher says that the first part of the name points to a challenge and the second part points to a tiger.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: if a word part means challenge, the meaning is about daring someone to try.
bridge.passage: Mina invited the strongest runner to a race and asked, 'Will you try?'
bridge.prompt: Which word best matches this action?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: read both the word meaning and the story setting. A strong answer explains the name, not only the animal.
masterclass.passage: The game name joins the idea of challenge with the tiger side in the game story.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer explains the full name best?
options: a challenge connected with the tiger
accepted_answers: a challenge connected with the tiger

independent_check.teaching_block: Now use the meaning without hints.
independent_check.passage: A new player asks what the first idea in Hekko tells us. The coach says it is about daring the other side to compete.
independent_check.prompt: Which word means daring someone to compete?

levels.title: Read team rules
levels.focus: identify roles and numbers in a game description
levels.teaching_goal: Find team names, player counts, and role rules in a game explanation.

guided_check.teaching_block: A rule paragraph often gives exact numbers. When a question asks 'how many', look for the number first.
guided_check.passage: Before a school game begins, each side chooses eleven players and stands in two groups.
guided_check.prompt: How many players are on each team?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: one team stays inside a circle by linking together; that link is called a chain.
bridge.passage: The inside team joins hands so the group can move and defend together.
bridge.prompt: What does the inside team make?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: separate the two team roles. One side protects the circle; the other side enters and tries to push players out.
masterclass.passage: Two outside players step in. The inside group holds together and tries not to cross the line.
masterclass.prompt: Which phrase describes the inside team's job?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now identify the rule without hints.
independent_check.passage: The inside team links arms so members can move as one group and avoid being pushed out.
independent_check.prompt: What does the inside team form?

levels.title: Understand surrender and scoring
levels.focus: connect special words to game events
levels.teaching_goal: Explain what a special game word means and when the game ends.

guided_check.teaching_block: A special word in a game can name an action. If a caught player says the word for giving up, it means surrender.
guided_check.passage: A player is surrounded by the other team and says the word that means giving up the turn.
guided_check.prompt: What does the player show by saying the surrender word?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: a game can end because players are out, players are caught, or time is over.
bridge.passage: The clock rang just as both teams were still playing.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: do not confuse score with end condition. Points decide who wins; end conditions decide when play stops.
masterclass.passage: One side had more points when the final signal was heard.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now use the end condition without hints.
independent_check.passage: Every player from the outside team has been caught, so no one from that side can enter again.

levels.title: Choose sound-alike words
levels.teaching_goal: Choose the correct spelling when two words sound alike but mean different things.

guided_check.teaching_block: There points to a place or begins a sentence about something existing. Their means belonging to them.
guided_check.passage: ___ is a wide playground near the school.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: their answers whose thing it is.
bridge.passage: The players kept ___ water bottles near the bench.
bridge.prompt: Choose the word that shows belonging.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: ask the meaning question. If it means the number, use two. If it means also or more than enough, use too.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now choose the correct sound-alike word without hints.
independent_check.passage: The team raised ___ flag after the game.

levels.title: Use simple past verbs
levels.teaching_goal: Use simple past tense to describe actions that already happened.

guided_check.teaching_block: For many regular verbs, add -ed to show the action happened earlier. Visit becomes visited.
guided_check.prompt: Choose the correct past tense verb.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: decide becomes decided when the action happened in the past.
bridge.passage: Yesterday, the captain ___ the batting order.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: some words only need -ed, but words ending in e usually take only d. Decide becomes decided.
masterclass.passage: The team ___ to practise one more time.

independent_check.teaching_block: Now write the past tense verb without hints.
independent_check.passage: Today I choose one game. Yesterday I ___ to watch Hekko.
independent_check.prompt: Write the past tense form of decide.
